findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments. The only definition in the repository is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160, and a grep finds no other overload. `UsernameForm` fails to compile, so the `services` module and everything after it fail to build. Pass the user: `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. The intent is to show the form instead of skipping it on re-authentication when passkeys are available.

findings.title: `user != null` condition removes passkeys from the normal (no user yet) login page
findings.body: The old code set up WebAuthn (`fillContextForm`) when `context.getUser() == null`, which is the normal first-visit login. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` now returns true only when `user != null`, and both call sites use it (lines 115 and 137). On a normal login the user is null, so `fillContextForm` is no longer called. The login page then has no `//form[@id='webauth']`, no conditional UI and no auto-login with a discoverable key. The same happens after a failed username/password attempt, because `challenge(context, error, field)` runs with the user cleared. The tests in this PR contradict the code. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:83-119) expects auto-login on first open. `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` expects the webauth form at line 146 before any user is selected. `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` expects it after `oauth.openLoginForm()` with no user. The condition probably needs to be `user == null || <re-authentication with passkeys allowed>`, not `user != null`. This also affects `UsernameForm` (via line 47) and `PasswordForm` and `IdpUsernamePasswordForm`, which extend `UsernamePasswordForm`.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys at realm level, so it does not test a user without a passkey
findings.body: The comment at line 277 says passkeys are not enabled for the realm. The comment at line 304 says passkeys should not appear "as this user does not have passkey". The test only sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so it only covers the realm-disabled case. Nothing tests a passkeys-enabled realm with a re-authenticating user who has no passkey. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` does not look at the user's credentials either. The test name and comments describe one behaviour and the test checks another.

findings.title: Missing @Override on overridden method
findings.body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides the method added in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` but has no `@Override`. Add the annotation so the compiler catches a signature drift.

contracts.action: UsernameForm.authenticate skips the form on re-authentication unless conditional passkeys are enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate (UsernamePasswordForm.java:86-120), which sets USERNAME_HIDDEN and the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note when the user is already set
contracts.before_after: Before, a pre-set user went straight to context.success(), unless the user had linked brokers. Now it should show the form when passkeys are on. As written, it calls a method that does not exist.
contracts.visible_effect: The module does not compile, so no user-visible behaviour.

contracts.action: Passkeys form setup is now gated by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user), which requires a non-null user
contracts.equivalent_path: The old inline condition `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` in challenge(); the old authenticate() block had the same check.
contracts.before_after: Before, the form was filled when the user was null (normal login). Now it is filled only when the user is non-null (re-authentication).
contracts.visible_effect: The first-visit login page loses the passkey form and conditional UI. After a failed username attempt the passkey form is also gone.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent loss of passkey login for the normal flow. Existing tests that expect the webauth form with no user would fail.

contracts.action: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError replaces the inline USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED setup in badPasswordHandler and is also called from the passkey error path
contracts.equivalent_path: AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:257-260), which is the same Boolean.parseBoolean of the auth note
contracts.before_after: The helper reads the same auth note and sets the same two form attributes as the old inline code. It is now also called from WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse, so a failed passkey during re-authentication keeps the username hidden.
contracts.visible_effect: The error page after a failed passkey during re-authentication shows the re-authentication layout instead of a username field.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. The auth note is set in authenticate() for a pre-set user and removed when there is none. The OrganizationAuthenticator also uses WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator but never sets the note, so the helper is a no-op there.

summary: Two blockers. `UsernameForm.java:47` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but only the one-argument version exists, so `services` does not compile. The one-argument version also requires `user != null`, which turns passkey setup off on the normal login page where no user is selected. The PR's own tests, such as `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey`, rely on that setup. I read the diff files and their callers but did not build or run anything. I also noted that `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` disables passkeys for the whole realm instead of testing a user who has no passkey, and that `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` lacks `@Override`.
